chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
“The least amount of camphor sufficient for the deceased is one and a half mithqal.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: And some cotton is prepared for him, and the shroud is prepared, which is a shirt, a waist-wrapper, a cloth by which his lower part is bound up to his hips, a wrapping cloth, a hibarah garment, and a turban. The following indicates that.

key_terms.الْكَافُورِ: camphor used in preparing the deceased
key_terms.عِمَامَةٌ: a turban included among the burial cloths
key_terms.قَمِيصٌ: a shirt forming part of the shroud
key_terms.مِئْزَرٌ: a waist-wrapper used in the shrouding
key_terms.مِثْقَالٌ: a weight measure, here used for the minimum quantity

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of camphor for the deceased, and what are the components of the kafan in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report gives a legal ruling regarding the minimum amount of camphor used for the deceased and mentions the items prepared for burial shrouding. It reflects the jurisprudential details of funerary rites in Shia tradition and the prescribed components of the kafan.
